Hepatovenous segment VII — part of the liver. Largest internal organ and gland (~1.5 kg), occupying the right hypochondrium and epigastrium beneath the diaphragm. Divided functionally into eight Couinaud segments.

facts.bloodSupply: Hepatic artery proper (~25% of flow, ~50% of oxygen) and hepatic portal vein (~75% of flow); drained by hepatic veins into the IVC
facts.innervation: Hepatic plexus (vagal and coeliac sympathetic fibres)

Anterior cusp of pulmonary valve — part of the heart. Four-chambered muscular pump in the middle mediastinum, enclosed in the pericardium, about the size of a closed fist (~300 g). Its apex lies in the left 5th intercostal space at the mid-clavicular line.
clinicalNote: Cardiac tamponade (fluid in the pericardium) presents with Beck’s triad: hypotension, raised JVP and muffled heart sounds.

facts.function: Pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs (right heart) and oxygenated blood to the body (left heart); ~5 L/min at rest
facts.bloodSupply: Right and left coronary arteries; venous drainage via the coronary sinus into the right atrium
facts.innervation: Cardiac plexus (sympathetic T1–T4 accelerates, vagus slows); intrinsic conduction system (SA node → AV node → bundle of His → Purkinje fibres)

Caudate lobe of liver — part of the liver. Largest internal organ and gland (~1.5 kg), occupying the right hypochondrium and epigastrium beneath the diaphragm. Divided functionally into eight Couinaud segments.
clinicalNote: Cirrhosis causes portal hypertension (varices, ascites, splenomegaly) and reduced synthetic function (low albumin, prolonged INR).

facts.function: Carbohydrate, lipid and protein metabolism; bile production; synthesis of albumin and clotting factors; detoxification and drug metabolism; storage of glycogen, iron, vitamins A, D, B12
facts.bloodSupply: Hepatic artery proper (~25% of flow, ~50% of oxygen) and hepatic portal vein (~75% of flow); drained by hepatic veins into the IVC
facts.innervation: Hepatic plexus (vagal and coeliac sympathetic fibres)

overview: Pear-shaped sac on the visceral surface of the liver storing and concentrating bile.

facts.function: Stores and concentrates bile; contracts after fatty meals (CCK)
facts.bloodSupply: Cystic artery (usually from the right hepatic artery)

overview: Largest lymphoid organ, in the left hypochondrium beneath ribs 9–11.
clinicalNote: Easily ruptured in blunt trauma to the left lower ribs; after splenectomy give vaccines against encapsulated bacteria.

facts.function: Filters blood, removes old red cells, stores platelets, mounts immune responses to blood-borne antigens
facts.bloodSupply: Splenic artery; drains via the splenic vein to the portal system

overview: Lymphoid mass in the lateral wall of the oropharynx between the palatoglossal and palatopharyngeal arches.
clinicalNote: Peritonsillar abscess (quinsy) deviates the uvula to the opposite side.

facts.function: First-line immune surveillance of ingested and inhaled antigens
facts.bloodSupply: Tonsillar branch of the facial artery

overview: Lymphoid mass in the lateral wall of the oropharynx between the palatoglossal and palatopharyngeal arches.
clinicalNote: Peritonsillar abscess (quinsy) deviates the uvula to the opposite side.

facts.function: First-line immune surveillance of ingested and inhaled antigens
facts.bloodSupply: Tonsillar branch of the facial artery

overview: Dilated sac at the origin of the thoracic duct, anterior to L1–L2.
clinicalNote: Enlarged (>1 cm), hard or fixed lymph nodes warrant investigation for infection or malignancy.

facts.function: Collects lymph (and chyle) from the lower body and gut
facts.drainage: Intestinal and lumbar lymph trunks

overview: Largest lymphatic vessel (~40 cm) returning lymph to the venous system.
clinicalNote: Injury (e.g. during oesophagectomy) causes chylothorax.

facts.drainage: Lymph from the whole body except the right upper quadrant (head, neck, thorax and right arm)
facts.course: Ascends through the aortic hiatus between the aorta and azygos, crosses to the left at T5, drains into the left venous angle (subclavian/internal jugular junction)

overview: Short trunk draining the right upper quadrant of the body.
clinicalNote: Enlarged (>1 cm), hard or fixed lymph nodes warrant investigation for infection or malignancy.

facts.drainage: Right side of the head, neck, thorax and right upper limb
facts.course: Empties into the right venous angle

overview: Root, body (two corpora cavernosa, one corpus spongiosum) and glans.

facts.function: Copulation and urination
facts.bloodSupply: Internal pudendal artery (deep and dorsal arteries)

overview: Oval gonad in the scrotum producing sperm and testosterone.
clinicalNote: Testicular torsion is a surgical emergency (6-hour window); lymph drains to para-aortic, not inguinal, nodes.

facts.function: Spermatogenesis (seminiferous tubules); testosterone (Leydig cells)
facts.bloodSupply: Testicular artery (from the aorta at L2)
facts.drainage: Pampiniform plexus → testicular vein (left into the left renal vein, right into the IVC)

overview: Muscular duct conveying sperm from the epididymis through the inguinal canal to the ejaculatory duct.
clinicalNote: Divided in vasectomy through a small scrotal incision.

facts.function: Transports sperm
facts.course: Spermatic cord → deep inguinal ring → crosses over the ureter → joins seminal vesicle duct

overview: Coiled gland behind the bladder.

facts.function: Produces ~60–70% of seminal fluid (fructose-rich)

overview: Air passage from the nostrils to the nasopharynx, divided by the nasal septum and lined by vascular mucosa with conchae.
clinicalNote: Most nosebleeds arise from Kiesselbach’s plexus (Little’s area) on the anterior septum.

facts.function: Warms, humidifies and filters inspired air; olfaction

overview: Voice box: cartilaginous skeleton (thyroid, cricoid, arytenoid, epiglottis) housing the vocal folds.
clinicalNote: Emergency airway: cricothyroidotomy through the cricothyroid membrane between the thyroid and cricoid cartilages.

facts.function: Phonation; protects the airway during swallowing
facts.bloodSupply: Superior and inferior laryngeal arteries

overview: Largest salivary gland, wrapped around the ramus of the mandible.
clinicalNote: The facial nerve branches run through the gland — at risk in parotid surgery; mumps causes parotid swelling.

facts.function: Serous saliva (amylase) into the mouth via the parotid (Stensen) duct opposite the 2nd upper molar
facts.innervation: Parasympathetic secretomotor fibres from CN IX via the otic ganglion
facts.bloodSupply: External carotid artery branches

facts.innervation: Parasympathetic secretomotor fibres from CN IX via the otic ganglion
facts.bloodSupply: External carotid artery branches

overview: Musculomembranous tube (naso-, oro- and laryngopharynx) shared by the respiratory and digestive tracts.

facts.function: Conducts air and food; swallowing

overview: Blind-ended pouch at the start of the large intestine in the right iliac fossa.

facts.function: Receives ileal contents; absorbs water and electrolytes
facts.bloodSupply: Ileocolic artery

overview: S-shaped mobile segment on its own mesentery, from the pelvic brim to S3.
clinicalNote: The commonest site of diverticular disease and of volvulus in the elderly.

facts.function: Stores faeces before defecation
facts.bloodSupply: Sigmoid arteries (IMA)
